But `auth: signature` plus `transport_security: mtls` says exactly that; auth is how the CALLER proves who it is, and here the caller is the gateway. What no field can say is the delegated half: the authenticated party (the gateway) is not the principal it vouches for. The field scopes that out on purpose, and it is the agent-plus-principal gap filed elsewhere in this report (I1/D1)","source":"art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29 (item I21, designer friction #13)","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-29, item I21 of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29.

① OBSERVED (friction #13, 0.74.0): "set_interface_spec `auth` enum has no value for 'a signed assertion from an upstream gateway, over mTLS'. Workaround: used `signature`/`mtls`, with the real mechanism in prose. Cost: fidelity only." The ikg router admits only requests carrying the flo2 gateway's signed caller identity, plus the set of designs that caller may see.

② PRECEDENT: searched in both designs. cap:interface-spec (realized) exists. No prior report on auth values.

③ CANDIDATES:
- (a) the enum lacks the mechanism;
- (b) the enum has it, and the designer's encoding was already right;
- (c) what is missing is not a mechanism but a second party: on whose behalf.

④⑤ MEASURED, schema/structure.yaml Interface.auth:
- values: none, api_key, oauth2, jwt, mtls, basic, signature, kerberos, physical, unspecified.
- description: "how the caller proves who it is — a mechanism, not a role... NOT AUTHORIZATION: which role or actor MAY use the interface has no field yet (req:vocabulary-covers-personnel, deferred)".
- transport_security separately has mtls.
The gateway proves itself by signature over mTLS, so `signature` plus `mtls` is the honest encoding: (a) is refuted and (b) holds. What the prose carried and no field can is (c): the signed assertion names an END USER (the principal) whom the gateway (the authenticated party) vouches for, together with that user's visible designs. auth is single-valued and single-party by design.

⑥ CLASS: not a missing enum value. It is the same agent-versus-principal gap as I1 and D1 in this report: provenance and approval cannot record "X acting for Y", and neither can a contract's auth. Adding an enum value would hide that behind a new word.

⑦⑧ Nothing to pin until the principal/agent modelling is decided. That is the D1 idea, owned by the authority cluster of this triage and not recorded here.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether an interface that accepts two mechanisms (oauth2 for agents, mTLS for services) needs auth to be multi-valued. The ikg design's public endpoints said oauth2 for both, so this report did not exercise it.","subject_id":"cap:interface-spec","valid_from":"2026-09-29"}
